sentences.zh: 而平章政事亮因群臣震恐，與所親駙馬唐括辯、寢殿小底大興國、護衛十人長忽土、阿里出虎等謀爲亂。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Grand Councilor Liang, because the ministers were terrified, plotted rebellion with his intimate, imperial son-in-law Tangguo Bian, sleeping-hall attendant Da Xingguo, guard squad leader of ten Hutu, Ali Chuhu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Grand Councilor Liang, seeing the court paralyzed by fear, conspired with his confidants—imperial son-in-law Tangguo Bian, sleeping-hall attendant Da Xingguo, guard squad leader Hutu, Ali Chuhu, and others.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以忽土、阿里出虎當內直，命省令史李老僧語興國。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Hutu and Ali Chuhu were assigned to inner duty; Provincial clerk Li Laoseng was ordered to speak with Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Hutu and Ali Chuhu were posted to inner palace duty, and provincial clerk Li Laoseng was sent to confer with Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 夜二鼓，興國竊符，矯詔開宮門，召辯等。

translations.literal: At the second watch of night, Xingguo stole the tally, forged an edict to open the palace gate, and summoned Bian and the others.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch Xingguo stole the tally, forged an edict to open the palace gate, and summoned Bian and the rest.

sentences.zh: 亮懷刀與其妹夫特廝隨辯入至宮門，守者以辯駙馬，不疑，內之。

translations.literal: Liang concealed a blade and followed Bian to the palace gate; the guards, seeing Bian was an imperial son-in-law, suspected nothing and admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Liang hid a blade and followed Bian to the palace gate; the guards, knowing Bian as imperial son-in-law, suspected nothing and let them in.

sentences.zh: 及殿門，衛士覺，抽刃劫之，莫敢動。

translations.literal: At the hall gate the guards noticed; they drew blades to seize them, but none dared move.
translations.idiomatic: At the hall gate the guards sensed trouble and drew blades to seize them—yet none dared act.

sentences.zh: 忽土、阿亮出虎至帝前，帝求榻上常所置佩刀，不知已爲興國易置其處，忽土、阿里出虎遂進弑帝，亮復前手刃之，血濺滿其面與衣。

translations.literal: When Hutu and Ali Chuhu reached the emperor, the emperor sought the personal blade he always kept by the couch, not knowing Xingguo had already switched its place; Hutu and Ali Chuhu then advanced and assassinated the emperor, and Liang stepped forward and stabbed him with his own hand—blood splashed over his face and clothes.
translations.idiomatic: When Hutu and Ali Chuhu reached the emperor, he groped for the blade he kept by the couch, not knowing Xingguo had already moved it; Hutu and Ali Chuhu struck first, and Liang stepped in to stab him himself—blood spattered his face and robes.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，時年三十一。

translations.literal: The emperor died; he was thirty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died at thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 左丞相秉德等遂奉亮坐，羅拜呼萬歲，立以爲帝。

translations.literal: Left Chief Councilor Bingde and the others thereupon supported Liang to the seat; they bowed in a circle and shouted “Long live!” and established him as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chief Councilor Bingde and the others thereupon seated Liang on the throne; they bowed in a circle, shouted “Long live the emperor!” and proclaimed him ruler.

sentences.zh: 降帝爲東昏王，葬于皇后裴滿氏墓中。

translations.literal: The late emperor was demoted to Prince of Eastern Darkness and buried in the tomb of Empress Peiman.
translations.idiomatic: The fallen emperor was demoted to Prince of Eastern Darkness and buried in Empress Peiman’s tomb.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，改葬爲大房山蓼香甸，諸王同兆域。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Zhenyuan era he was reburied at Liaoxiangdian on Great Fang Mountain, sharing a tomb precinct with the princes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Zhenyuan era he was reburied at Liaoxiangdian on Great Fang Mountain, in a tomb precinct shared with the princes.

sentences.zh: 大定初，追諡武靈皇帝，廟號閔宗，陵曰思陵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dading era he was posthumously titled Emperor Wuling, given the temple name Minzong, and his mausoleum was called Siling.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dading era he received the posthumous title Emperor Wuling, the temple name Minzong, and the mausoleum name Siling.

sentences.zh: 別立廟。

translations.literal: A separate temple was established.
translations.idiomatic: A separate ancestral temple was established for him.

sentences.zh: 十九年，升祔爲太廟，增諡弘基纘武莊靖孝成皇帝。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and his posthumous title was augmented to Emperor Hongji Zuowu Zhuangjing Xiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and his posthumous title was augmented to Hongji Zuowu Zhuangjing Xiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，改廟號熙宗。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year his temple name was changed to Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year his temple name was changed to Xizong.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，以思陵狹小，改葬于峨眉穀，仍號思陵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, because Siling was too cramped, he was reburied in Emei Valley, still called Siling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, because Siling was too cramped, he was reburied in Emei Valley, retaining the mausoleum name Siling.

sentences.zh: 詔中外。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to the court and the realm.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was promulgated throughout the court and the realm.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：熙宗之時，四方無事，敬禮宗室大臣，委以國政，其繼體守文之治，有足觀者。

translations.literal: Eulogy: In Xizong’s time the four quarters were untroubled; he treated the imperial clan and great ministers with respect and entrusted them with state affairs—his succession in holding to the civil way is worth regard.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: In Xizong’s day the realm was untroubled; he honored the imperial clan and great ministers and entrusted them with government—his civil succession is worth regard.

sentences.zh: 末年酗酒妄殺，人懷危懼。

translations.literal: In his later years he drank to excess and killed at whim; men lived in dread.
translations.idiomatic: In his final years he drank to excess and killed at whim, until the court lived in dread.

sentences.zh: 所謂前有讒而不見，後有賊而不知。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by having slander before one yet not seeing it, and having a traitor behind yet not knowing it.
translations.idiomatic: So it was said: slander stood before him yet he did not see it; treachery stood behind him yet he did not know it.

sentences.zh: 馴致其禍，非一朝一夕故也。

translations.literal: To tame and bring on his calamity was not the work of a morning or an evening.
translations.idiomatic: His fall was not the work of a single morning or evening—it had been long in the making.
